scene: A shopkeeper leans forward in her doorway and opens both arms wide, palms turned up, chin lifted and head tilted back in a questioning shrug. Baskets of fruit flank the step beside her. Warm afternoon light floods the open shopfront.

A young woman bows deeply from the waist, folded almost double, hugging a battered leather wallet against her chest with both arms. A traffic policeman in a white helmet stands still behind her. Rain slicks the street corner; headlights glare off the wet tarmac.

A young man lunges across a bar table with both hands cupped around his mouth, head thrown forward, shouting toward the far side of the room. Bottles and glasses crowd the table under him. A dim crowded bar at night, coloured lights behind.

A lawyer standing at the head of a long table rips the bottom sheet clean off a stapled contract, the torn strip curling in his raised fist. Seated figures around the table sit frozen, smiles stuck. Cold boardroom light, city glass behind.

A woman holds one hand up close to the camera and pinches her thumb and forefinger almost shut, a single flake of dried red chilli caught between the fingertips. Her face behind the hand is screwed up in alarm. Plain blurred background, soft daylight.

A foreman in a hard hat throws one arm straight up overhead, thumb raised toward a control booth above the factory floor. A conveyor of parts grinds past below him. Cold overhead lamps, oil-stained concrete, machinery haze.

A man crouches at the edge of a shallow stream and lowers a flat stepping stone into the water with both hands. A line of stones already reaches halfway to the far bank. Morning mist over the reeds, soft grey light on the water.

A tea vendor tilts a battered dented pot and pours a fresh glass from the same spent leaves, steam curling off the stream. A strainer heaped with used leaves and two drained glasses stand beside her. Sunlit street beyond the stall.

A small boy snatches a roasting chestnut off a glowing brazier and flings his hand up into the air, fingers still clamped around it, face screwed up. Coals glow orange beneath the grill. Night, sparks lifting, dark street behind him.

A woman lowers a small iced cake with both hands onto a white lace doily inside a glass-fronted cake stand. A stack of hand-cut doilies, scissors and paper scraps lie on the counter beside her. Bright flat shop light.

A woman at a small cafe table slams a heavy grey river stone down onto the tabletop, her arm still straight, her head turned firmly aside, eyebrows raised. Coffee cups jump on their saucers. Bright window light behind her.

A man stands in the middle of a tiny flat with both arms out at his sides, palms flat against the opposite walls without straightening his elbows. A folded bed and a single hotplate are crammed in behind him. Grey light from one narrow window.

A farmer under a heavy mango tree throws both arms out wide in a huge shrug, shoulders up to his ears, chin tipped back toward the half-ripe fruit overhead. An empty wooden crate sits at his feet. Hot hazy light through the leaves.

A baker stretches up on his toes to slide a tray of pale rolls onto the top shelf of a tall steel cooling rack, every shelf below it bare. A dark window behind him, flour dust hanging in the lamplight.

A hotel clerk reaches high above her head and lifts a key off a hook on a board of hanging keys, her whole body stretched up. A guest's suitcase stands alone on the floor by the desk. Warm lobby lamplight.

A man in a suit stands over an empty steel serving tray with his arms hanging and his shoulders dropped, staring down at the tongs lying across bare smeared metal. Stacked chairs and emptied trays fill the hall behind him. Cold strip lighting.

A woman holds a single prawn out at arm's length over an open bin, her whole body leaning away, face turned aside. A tray of prawns sits on the counter behind her. Harsh white light spills from an open fridge into the dark kitchen.

A crow on a cafe railing leans right forward toward a plate of chips, beak wide open, wings half lifted from its body, one foot raised off the rail. Bright overcast light, the sea flat and grey beyond the terrace.

A young clerk bows deeply from the waist, holding a closed file out ahead of him in both hands. A robed elder stands motionless in front of him. Dark panelled walls, a brass lamp, one high window throwing a shaft of light.

A magician sweeps a red cloth up and off a table with one arm flung overhead, the cloth still flying, a brass birdcage standing revealed on the bare tabletop. Footlights glare up at him; the auditorium behind is pitch dark.

A boy levers the lid off a tin of bright blue paint with a screwdriver, both hands straining, the lid tipping up and paint glinting underneath. Open tins of red, yellow and green stand in a row beside him. Bright hardware-shop light.

A camp cook swings a brimming ladle of steaming rice porridge out over a row of tin bowls, arm fully extended, apron flapping. A line of sleepy workers stands waiting behind the bowls, breath showing. First grey light over the field camp.

A woman leans over a kitchen counter with both palms flat on it, face low, watching a small hourglass timer whose sand is halfway run through. A squat teapot steams beside it. Bright morning light across the worktop.

A heavily built man in a vest swings a mallet down onto the pad of a fairground high striker, arms following through, the puck streaking up the tower and the brass bell at the top jolting sideways. Night, strings of coloured bulbs.

A man in a suit crawls on hands and knees half under a dining table, his neck yanked sideways and his head pinned low because his necktie is trapped beneath a table leg. A dropped coin lies just beyond his fingers. Low angle, warm lamplight.

A curator lifts a tall specimen jar holding a pale suspended lung off a dim museum shelf, raising it to her chest in both gloved hands. A shorter jar holding a heart stands in the gap beside it. Low warm display light.

A woman in a fitted scarlet dance dress stands in a dressing-room doorway with both arms raised above her head, turning on one heel so the skirt swings wide. A rail of costumes and a dressmaker's dummy crowd the room behind her. Bare bulbs.

A teacher in a neat uniform strides along a line of pupils with her hands clasped behind her back and her chin up, inspecting each face as she passes. The children stand still and straight-backed. Dusty schoolyard, green trees, hard morning light.

A farmer leaning on a milking-shed gatepost throws one arm up high, counting. One cow stands square in the open gateway with her head turned back, refusing to move; the rest of the herd crowds the lit shed behind her. Dusk, mud, warm lamplight.

A woman leans far out of the window of a moving railway carriage with one arm raised high in a wave, mouth open mid-note, hair blowing back. The emptying platform slides away behind her. Dusk, lamps coming on along the track.

An old carpenter leans over a boy at a sawhorse, his weathered hands closed over the boy's on the saw handle, driving the blade down through a half-cut plank. Sawdust curls in a shaft of light from a grimy workshop window.

A young tenant presses a folded stack of banknotes down into the open palm of an elderly landlady, leaning in with both hands. The landlady stands still in the shophouse doorway, a ring of keys hanging from her other fist. Dusk, warm doorway light.

A man sprawls asleep on his back beneath a coconut palm, hat over his face, arms flung out in the dust. A large green coconut hangs frozen in the air a hand's width above his chest. Harsh noon glare, hard black shadows.

A small woman in an apron balances a coconut on one upturned palm and taps its middle with the spine of a cleaver, the shell splitting cleanly into two halves. Abandoned hammers, a rock and scattered husk fibres litter the outdoor kitchen floor. Bright daylight.

A tall father in a work shirt strides through a packed night market gripping a small girl's wrist, towing her along as her feet skip to keep up. Stalls and strings of bulbs blur past on either side. Seen from behind, warm night light.

A geologist crouching in an open field holds up a long cylindrical soil core banded in coloured layers, turning it in both gloved hands. An enormous low moon fills the sky behind him. His head torch throws a hard white beam across the core.
